entry.title: Tax Fulfilment Date, Tax Reporting date

Dear all,

I am facing an issue with the Tax Fulfilment Date and Tax Reporting Date during credit memo creation.

entry.title: New Italian VAT references (Testo Unico IVA D.Lgs. 10/2026)
entry.content:
Dear Community,

Starting from January 1, 2027, Legislative Decree No. 10 of 2026 will come into force, introducing the new Consolidated VAT Act (Testo Unico IVA). This requires updating the legal references associated with the tax codes currently in use. To avoid creating from scratch all the many tax codes currently used in Italy, which would also involve a series of related activities, such as the determination of the TTX1 condition in documents and the alignment with third-party systems interfaced with SAP, our plan is simply to change the descriptions of the existing tax codes.

This raises an issue. As far as I know, there is no way to define a validity period for these texts. So if I change a tax code description, the new text applies to every document I print after the change. The problem arises in particular with the printing of the VAT registers, both for the periodic VAT return for the last month of the year, filed in January 2027, and for the annual VAT return, filed later in 2027. In this case, if I print the registers in 2027 after changing all the descriptions, transactions posted in 2026 will show the new description.

My question is therefore: has SAP planned, or does it already provide, a solution to this temporal mismatch between the period of the transaction and its description?

I couldn't find any info on the topic, apart from one improvement request for SAP Business ONE, but, considering my question, basically unrelated.

I know I'm romantic thinking that there could be something about it, but you never know.

Are you having the same problem? How did you cope with? I am on a Cloud Public multitenant version beware.

Thanks

Peter

entry.title: Mapping SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition User Licensing Types: Legacy (Core/Advanced) vs. New Subscr
entry.content:
Hi SAP Community,

We are currently working on a sizing and licensing estimation for a SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition project, and we need clarity on how the legacy user licensing model maps to the newer subscription model.

In our TDD (Test Data Directory) / Test Environment, we have the legacy user classification:

  1. Self-Service
  2. Core
  3. Advanced

However, for the client's target environment, we are working with the newer user subscription types:

  1. Self-Service
  2. Operational
  3. Finance Base
  4. SCM Base
  5. SAP Finance Base & SCM Base
  6. Finance Premium
  7. SCM Premium

Our specific questions:

  1. How does the legacy Core user map to the new breakdown? Does Core map strictly to Operational, or do Finance Base and SCM Base also count as Core?
  2. How does the legacy Advanced user map to the new breakdown? Does Advanced only correlate to the Premium tiers (Finance Premium, SCM Premium), or are Finance Base and SCM Base considered Advanced?

Since the standard roles in our TDD environment report either "Core" or "Advanced", we want to ensure we don't overestimate or classify everything as Advanced in the customer's production/subscription environment.

Any official SAP documentation, mapping matrix, or guidance on this equivalency would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you in advance!

entry.title: Austria - Down Payment Process in SAP Cloud ERP
entry.content:
Dear SAP Community,

when processing Down Payment Requests (FAZ) in Sales & Distribution in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud, a tax compliance challenge arises in countries like Austria: the tax on a FAZ should be treated as deferred (latent), separate from the tax on a standard invoice (F2) or credit memo (LR).

The standard scope item BJK uses condition type TTX1 with access sequence TTX1, which includes an access to condition table A165 – but this access is controlled by Requirement 8, which only fires for export scenarios where departure country differs from destination country. For domestic scenarios like AT→AT, the system falls through to the next access and picks up the same tax code regardless of billing document type – meaning a Down Payment Request (Billing Category P) gets the same tax treatment as a final invoice.

This makes it impossible out of the box to assign a deferred tax code specifically to FAZ documents in domestic scenarios, while keeping the standard tax code for F2 and LR. The Billing Category field exists in condition table A165 as a key field, but the export requirement blocks it from being used in domestic cases.

Has anyone solved this for Austria in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition?

  • Did you go the custom access sequence route?
  • Is there a standard SAP solution we might be missing?
  • Any experience with SAP Support on this topic? 

Any input is highly appreciated! 🙏

entry.title: Manage Purchase Orders: custom item field visibility via MM_PUR_S4_PO_FLDCNTRL_SIMPLE
entry.content:
Hello experts,

System: SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition
App: Manage Purchase Orders (F0842A)

Requirement:
A custom checkbox on the product master ("Trade Fields Mandatory") controls
4 custom PO item fields (business context Procurement: Purchasing Document Item).
- Indicator = Yes -> fields visible and mandatory
- Indicator = No -> fields hidden

Implementation (Custom Logic):
- MM_PUR_S4_PO_FLDCNTRL_SIMPLE: reads the indicator from I_Product for
purchaseorderitem-material and sets fieldstatus '+' or '-' for the 4 fields
- MM_PUR_S4_PO_MODIFY_ITEM: clears the fields when indicator = No
- BD_MMPUR_FINAL_CHECK_PO: blocks saving when indicator = Yes and fields are empty

Issue:
1. PO with item 10 (product A, indicator Yes) and item 20 (product B, indicator No):
the item object page keeps the visibility of the previously displayed item.
2. Changing the material of an existing item (B -> A or A -> B): the fields keep
the visibility of the old material.
3. Browser refresh (F5 / Ctrl+F5) does not correct it. Only after opening
Adapt UI and refreshing is the correct visibility shown.

Checks done:
- BAdI returns the correct field status per item (verified)
- Only one published implementation per BAdI
- Product saved (not in draft) before testing
- Tested with new PO drafts after clearing browser cache
- UI adaptation version created and activated

Field control code (simplified):

LOOP AT fieldselection_table ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs>).
IF to_upper( <fs>-field ) CS 'YY1_TRADEPROGRAM_PDI' " + 3 more fields
<fs>-fieldstatus = lv_status. " '+' or '-'
ENDIF.
ENDLOOP.

Questions:
1. Is this a known limitation of Manage Purchase Orders, i.e. dynamic field
control for custom item fields is not re-evaluated per item or after a
material change?
2. Is there a recommended way (side effect, setting or other BAdI) to force
the item page to re-apply the field control?
3. Has anyone implemented product-dependent visibility of custom PO item
fields successfully in Public Cloud?

Screenshots attached.
Thank you!

entry.title: How to Exclude a condition type from Accounting in Intercompany Billing?
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

I have a requirement in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud to exclude condition type ZTPR from accounting and consider only the preceding condition types PCIP and ZI02 for accounting.

I configured the pricing procedure as follows:

  • Marked ZTPR as statistical.
  • Removed the account key from ZTPR.
  • Assigned account keys to PCIP and ZI02.

However, during Intercompany Billing, ZTPR is active and the statistical indicator is not set in the billing document. Because of this, the preceding conditions PCIP and ZI02 become inactive and are not considered for accounting.

I tested the same pricing procedure in a normal sales and billing process, where it works as expected. ZTPR remains statistical and the other conditions remain active.

The issue occurs only during the IC billing process.

My expected accounting behavior is:

  • PCIP → Accounting relevant
  • ZI02 → Accounting relevant
  • ZTPR → Not accounting relevant
At the same time, ZTPR is used in another pricing procedure, so any proposed solution should not impact its existing behavior in that sales process.

Could you please help clarify the following?

  1. Is this the standard behavior for intercompany billing in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud?
  2. Why is the statistical indicator maintained for ZTPR not reflected in the IC billing document?
  3. Is there any standard configuration or supported approach to prevent ZTPR from being relevant for accounting while keeping PCIP and ZI02 active and relevant for accounting?
  4. Is there any specific restriction related to statistical conditions in the intercompany pricing procedure that needs to be considered?

I have attached the pricing procedure screenshot for reference.

Thanks in advance for your support.
